title: The Return of a Discredited Pseudoscience
gist: Science writer Dan Falk argues that eugenics—the discredited notion that selective breeding can improve the human race, pioneered by Francis Galton—is resurfacing in contemporary politics and culture a century after its heyday.

insights.claim: The author asserts that eugenics—the pseudoscientific belief that nature has a 'right' combination of genes and that selective breeding can improve the human race—is making a comeback in today's political and cultural environment, a century after its historical peak.
insights.speaker: Dan Falk
insights.so_what: Flags a resurgence of eugenics-adjacent rhetoric in politics/culture as a live social trend worth tracking, though the article's supporting specifics are cut off by the paywall.
insights.quote: Eugenics is rearing its ugly head again in today's crucible of politics and culture

insights.claim: Eugenics traces to Francis Galton, Charles Darwin's cousin, who extended Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace's evolutionary biology work by proposing that, just as farmers selectively breed animals, humans could be guided toward producing 'better' offspring.
insights.speaker: Dan Falk
insights.so_what: Provides the historical intellectual origin of eugenics as a pseudoscience derived from a distortion of Darwinian evolutionary theory.
insights.quote: other thinkers, like Darwin's cousin, Francis Galton, took things further by supposing that, just as farmers breed animals to improve or weed out various traits, humans could be guided to make 'better' offspring
